t.E285.agn: In the body it is evaluated as boron, in the same way as boric acid. In 2013 EFSA set a group ADI of 0.16 mg/kg body weight, expressed as boron, for boric acid and borax; adverse effects on the male reproductive system have been reported in animal studies. EFSA stated that regular exceedance of the ADI from the authorised use in caviar alone is unlikely.
t.E285.body: It is absorbed as a boron compound.
t.E285.eff.0.a: Regular exceedance of the daily limit (unlikely from the authorised use in caviar alone)
t.E285.eff.0.t: Adverse effects on the male reproductive system and on development were seen in animal studies; the daily limit is based on these findings
t.E285.eff.0.w: Animal studies; relevant to development during pregnancy
t.E285.eval: In the EU it is authorised only for caviar (sturgeon roe). Borax (disodium tetraborate) is classified as toxic for reproduction Category 1B in the EU CLP classification (H360FD; Regulation 790/2009). In 2013 EFSA set the group ADI for boric acid and borax at 0.16 mg/kg body weight/day, expressed as boron.
t.E285.prod: Obtained by grinding sodium borate ore, dissolving it in hot water and crystallising it (a physical process).
t.E285.pw.0: It contains sodium; sodium from the additive at the permitted level in caviar is usually less than that from salt.
t.E285.regx.0: Re-evaluated together with boric acid; group ADI 0.16 mg boron/kg body weight/day.
t.E285.regx.1: Only in sturgeon roe (caviar), at most 4,000 mg/kg expressed as boric acid.
t.E285.summary: A boron-containing mineral salt (borax). In the EU it is authorised in food only in sturgeon caviar.
t.E285.what: Sodium tetraborate (borax); it is used together with boric acid as a preservative in caviar.
